cards.explanation: The answer is that David asks whether God will forget him forever. He says, "Will You forget me forever?" (Psalm 13:1). He doesn't dress it up first. I think it took real nerve to say that straight to the LORD.

The answer is his enemy. David asks, "How long will my enemy dominate me?" (Psalm 13:2). The psalm never says who this enemy is. The enemy shows up again in verse 4, so I think he's weighing on David's mind.

The answer is True, friends. David asks the LORD, "Give light to my eyes, lest I sleep in death…" (Psalm 13:3). Notice he's asking, not demanding. He calls Him "…O LORD my God." right before it, and I think that says a lot about who he's turning to.

The answer is False. Instead of mourning, David says, "and my foes rejoice when I fall." (Psalm 13:4). A foe who sends flowers would be a nice change, but that's not this psalm. Their cheering is exactly what David doesn't want.

The answer is the LORD's loving devotion, friends. David says, "But I have trusted in Your loving devotion…" (Psalm 13:5). He asked all those hard questions, and then he said where his trust is. It's a short turn, but it changes the whole psalm.

The answer is heart, friends. David says, "my heart will rejoice in Your salvation." (Psalm 13:5). Back in verse 2 he had sorrow in his heart each day. Now that same heart is the one that will rejoice.

The answer is that the LORD has been good to him, bakers. David says, "I will sing to the LORD, for He has been good to me." (Psalm 13:6). His reason is the LORD's goodness. I think that's worth remembering the next time a hard day tries to talk loud.
